functions.name: NewReader
functions.summary: NewReader returns a new ReadCloser that can be used to read the uncompressed version of r. If r does not also implement [io.ByteReader], the decompressor may read more data than necessary from r. The reader returns [io.EOF] after the final block in the DEFLATE stream has been encountered. Any trailing data after the final block is ignored.

functions.name: NewReaderDict
functions.summary: NewReaderDict is like [NewReader] but initializes the reader with a preset dictionary. The returned reader behaves as if the uncompressed data stream started with the given dictionary, which has already been read. NewReaderDict is typically used to read data compressed by [NewWriterDict].

functions.name: NewWriter
functions.summary: NewWriter returns a new [Writer] compressing data at the given level. Following zlib, levels range from 1 ([BestSpeed]) to 9 ([BestCompression]); higher levels typically run slower but compress more. Level 0 ([NoCompression]) does not attempt any compression; it only adds the necessary DEFLATE framing. Level -1 ([DefaultCompression]) uses the default compression level. Level -2 ([HuffmanOnly]) will use Huffman compression only, giving a very fast compression for all types of input, but sacrificing considerable compression efficiency.

functions.name: NewWriterDict
functions.summary: NewWriterDict is like [NewWriter] but initializes the new [Writer] with a preset dictionary. The returned [Writer] behaves as if the dictionary had been written to it without producing any compressed output. The compressed data written to w can only be decompressed by a reader initialized with the same dictionary (see [NewReaderDict]).
